newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan ends higher against US dollar in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Yuan ends higher against US dollar in Shanghai.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed up at 8.2907 on Thursday from Wednesday's 8.2920 against the U.S. dollar due to active buying late in trading, traders said.
The weighted average price on Wednesday was 8.2920.
Dealers said active buying was seen pushing the yuan higher late in trading on market expectations that China would post a strong foreign trade surplus for the first half of 1997.
Beijing is due to announce the first half foreign trade data this weekend.
The yuan opened slightly up at 8.2918 and moved around the 8.2920 level for most of the session.
It hit an intraday low of 8.2950 around the mid-session and rose in the last 30 minutes of trading to hit its intraday high of 8.2900 several times, traders said.
Trading was more active than on Wednesday with most business done at about 8.2915, traders said.
One dealer said buying had emerged, after the yuan had moved in a narrow range around 8.2920 in the past few trading days, on expectations of a strong trade surplus.

"Some bankers believe the surplus in the first half of this year will be very strong against the same 1996 period, supporting the yuan's uptrend," he said. "This saw them do some heavy buying in late trading today."
A second dealer said selling pressure at the key 8.2900 resistance level was heavy despite the yuan having hit that level a number of times on Thursday.
The yuan would continue to move at high levels on Friday but could meet resistance at 8.2900, dealers said.
The yuan ended up at 7.3468 from 7.3516 against 100 Japanese yen and down at 1.0703 from 1.0700 vs the Hong Kong dollar.
